title: Katsu Curry
subtitle: Japanese curry sauce with a breaded chicken cutlet and rice
excerpt: The mild, golden Japanese curry that has become one of Britain's favourite Japanese restaurant dishes: a thick, aromatic curry sauce made from onions, carrots, apple, and curry powder, poured over a crisp panko-breaded chicken breast on a bed of short-grain rice.

recipe.sourceNotes: Japanese curry (kare) arrived in Japan via the British Royal Navy in the late nineteenth century, imported along with the British adaptation of Indian spices. The Japanese version evolved into something entirely its own: milder, sweeter, and thicker than either Indian or British curry, built on a roux and seasoned with shop-bought curry roux blocks or a simple spice blend. Katsu curry (katsu meaning cutlet) combines the curry sauce with a tonkatsu-style breaded cutlet, most commonly chicken. The dish became a British restaurant staple in the 1990s and 2000s and is now among the most ordered Japanese dishes in the UK. The sauce is made with a flour-and-butter roux thickened with stock, sweetened with apple and onion, and seasoned with curry powder.

content.text: The curry sauce is mild and sweet by design: do not add chilli or expect heat. The apple is classic and essential for the Japanese curry flavour; leave it in. Make the sauce ahead and reheat it just before serving; it thickens as it stands and may need a splash of stock to loosen. Pound the chicken breasts to an even 1.5 cm thickness so they cook evenly.

items.preparation: for breading; plus 2 tbsp for the sauce
peeled and grated; for sweetness in the sauce

content.text: Make the sauce: cook the onion and carrot in the butter over low heat for 15 minutes until very soft and golden. Add the garlic and curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Stir in 2 tablespoons of flour and cook for 1 minute. Add the grated apple. Gradually add the stock, whisking, then simmer for 15 minutes until thickened. Add the soy sauce. Blend until smooth with a hand blender if you prefer a smooth sauce.

Bread the chicken: coat each breast in seasoned flour, dip in beaten egg, and press into the panko. Heat the oil in a frying pan to 170 C and fry the breaded chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack.
Serve the rice in a bowl, add a sliced cutlet alongside, and pour the warm curry sauce over both. Garnish with shredded pickled ginger if available.
